title: Muru and the Sparkle Sneeze
markdown:
The warm sun shone on a mossy path through the Whispering Lantern Woods. Muru was a young ogre, skin green like moss, heart warm like the sun. He walked slowly. He liked these quiet times. Light through the leaves made little gold dots. The world made a low hum. Muru hummed too, like gentle thunder far away. He loved the leaves’ whisper in a soft wind, and little bugs buzzing.

He lived in the Wobblecap Mountains, where cottages sat like sleepy hats. These woods were his favourite place. Fuzzy caterpillars chewing slowly, as if leaves were a long story. Glow-bugs blinking like shy stars as the day grew softer. He always walked carefully. Big soft feet on moss. He did not want to disturb the quiet peace, or the glow-bugs’ game of now-you-see-me.

A little sputtering sound tickled his floppy ears, like a water beetle trying to whistle. Then a small fizzing pop. Muru peeked behind a big soft mushroom, cap deep earthy brown. In a patch of clover: a creature he had never seen. A little dragon, no bigger than his two hands together. Scales like a rainbow soap bubble, catching the fading sun, flashing little bright lights. It was sneezing. Each sneeze a puff of golden sparks. Sparks in puddles: a delightful fizz, a tiny puff of steam that tickled Muru’s nose. Sneeze. Fizz. Sneeze. Fizz. The little nose wiggled with each spark.

Muru blinked his big kind eyes. Very surprised. The dragon looked a little wobbly, as if it had just woken up. Sparkly sneezes like tiny hiccups of surprise. A gentle flutter in Muru’s chest, a warm feeling. How did such a tiny sparkly thing get all alone in these big woods? Tumbled from a nest? Wandered from its mama?

“Hello?” Soft and low, gentle thunder far away.

The dragon turned. Big curious eyes blinked slowly. Another sneeze. Sparks on a dewdrop on clover: a tiny diamond. Muru smiled, kind eyes crinkling. “You seem a little lost.” Warm low rumble. He must help this little creature home. Very carefully, a big mossy hand, fingers spread wide and gentle. The dragon looked, then rubbed its nose against warm fingers. Scales smooth and warm. Muru scooped it up. Warm smooth pebbles from a river. A tiny heart thrumming in his hand.

“I think I’ll call you Pip.” The name felt just right. Pip wiggled happily, a soft puff of sparks that tickled Muru’s chin. A chuckle. Pip’s sneezes were little bursts of sunshine. Puddles danced. Tiny wildflowers seemed to giggle. Along the mossy path, sparks lit the darkening woods into a wonderland of soft light. They found a patch of moon-moth silk, pearly, spun between two tall blades of grass, light as a whispered secret.

Pip nestled against Muru’s chest. Not just lost. A little lonely too. Muru wanted him safe and loved. A gentle pat. A soft rumbling purr, a tiny warm motor.

The sun dipped behind the Wobblecaps. Pink and purple. Shadows stretched like sleepy giants. A gentle worry: get Pip home safely, get home before the moon was too high, before the woods grew too dark.

The path split many ways into growing dark. Muru wasn’t sure. Pip sensed the worry, a little whimper like a tiny sigh. Sparks dimmed, little embers fading.

Muru sat on moss, Pip in his lap. A little helpless. Could he help Pip find home? Were they truly lost? Then he remembered the happy spark-filled sneezes, the dancing puddles, the giggling flowers. Pip needed comfort. “It’s okay, little Pip. We’ll figure this out together.” Close. Warmth and a gentle rumble, a promise, a soft low lullaby.

Then Pip sneezed. Not a fizzing shower. A soft warm glow, wrapping Muru like a cozy hug, a woolen blanket. As the glow pulsed, Pip pointed his tiny snout. That direction felt familiar. A happy sigh. Relief.

Muru followed the glow toward a clearing. A warm light flickered. Cormac, the goblin jam-maker, tending a small cheerful fire that crackled softly. From behind him, a soft worried coo. A much bigger dragon, scales like polished amber in the firelight, big eyes searching. Pip wiggled, a happy squeak. Muru nudged. Pip tumbled into mama’s waiting embrace. Nuzzles, soft rumbling. Pip sneezed a shower of happy strong sparks, a thousand tiny dancing fireflies.

Muru watched, heart full of quiet joy. A warm glow through him, like cocoa already, though the mug was still at home. He waved goodbye to Pip and mama, and to Cormac, who offered a warm gooey berry bun, sweetness in the air, jam still warm from the pot. Homeward, lanterns in the woods a little brighter, a comforting beacon along the moss. Pine needles and sweet berries. He thought of Pip’s warm sneezes and of helping, and of a mama dragon’s coo that had found the right clearing after all. Soon, home. A mug of warm sweet cocoa on the bedside table, steam like a gentle lullaby. Soft mossy bed. The room’s glow like Pip’s sparks. He drifted, dreaming of gentle adventures, a fire, and a bun that still tasted of jam. In the dream, Pip sneezed once more, politely, and the puddles fizzed goodnight.
characters: Muru (young ogre), Pip (little dragon), Cormac (goblin jam-maker)
